title: Numbers & Place Value

scenes.t: Every number lives in a house with rooms: thousands, hundreds, tens and ones. Each digit's place tells its value.
In 9345, the 9 means 9000, the 3 means 300, the 4 means 40 and the 5 means 5. So 9345 = 9000 + 300 + 40 + 5.
Two thousand, one hundred and sixteen is written 2116. And 1094 is one thousand and ninety-four.
To make the LARGEST number from cards 8, 9 and 7, put the biggest digit first: 987. For the smallest, put the smallest first: 789.
To order numbers, compare the number of digits first, then compare from the left. 16, 40, 46, 64, 106 goes from smallest to largest.
A sequence follows a rule. 135, 145, 155… adds 10 each time, so the next numbers are 165 and 175.

items.a: The value of a digit depends on its place.
